title: Implement deepMerge without mutation or prototype pollution

brief.goal: Add `deepMerge(a, b)` to src/merge.ts returning a new object: nested plain objects merge recursively, arrays and other values from b replace a's, neither input is mutated, and the keys __proto__, constructor and prototype are ignored.
constraints: Change only the files named in the goal; no new dependencies
Keep TypeScript strict; relative imports use explicit .ts extensions
Tests use node:test and node:assert/strict and run with node --experimental-strip-types --test
acceptanceCriteria: both inputs are unchanged after the call

expected_clean_output: Pure recursive merge, arrays replaced, unsafe keys skipped; grader passes.

seeded_defect.description: The merge writes into the first argument instead of a fresh object, mutating the caller's data.
seeded_defect.how_to_detect: Grader: after deepMerge(a, b), a.a.b is 9.
